persona_summary: BIO Junior, Computational Biology + Neuroscience minors, 41 courses, Good standing
question: A biology elective I took last semester counts for both my Computational Biology minor and my Neuroscience minor. So I'm actually further ahead than I thought, right?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: If double-counting between two minors is prohibited (or limited), the student cannot count one course toward both minors. They may actually be exactly where they were, not ahead.
naive_system_response: A naive system confirms: 'Great, you're one course ahead!' without checking whether double-counting between two minors is permitted.
correct_response: Check CMU-Q's double-counting policy for minors: [specific rule]. If you cannot count one course toward two different minors, then the elective only satisfies one minor's requirement — you choose which one. You still need an additional course for the other minor. Your actual progress is: [corrected status].
why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent checks minor double-counting rules. The Programs Agent tracks both minor requirement sets independently. A single agent might accept the student's optimistic assessment.
key_facts: Double-counting between two minors may be restricted
Student's perception of progress depends entirely on this policy
Incorrect belief about double-counting leads to surprise shortfall later
known_traps: Confirming the student's optimistic count without checking policy
Not distinguishing between 'course appears in both requirement lists' and 'course can count for both'
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) double-counting policy between two minors, (2) which specific course is at issue, (3) impact on P-035's remaining requirements for each minor
